summary: CoSN argues that E‑Rate should remain active, expanded to include permanent cybersecurity and redundant connectivity, and that it should not be conditioned on parental opt‑outs for screen‑based instruction. CoSN argues that E‑Rate should not be limited or sunset, citing its continued necessity for broadband, cybersecurity, and equity, and urges permanent inclusion of cybersecurity as an eligible service. CoSN argues for permanent cybersecurity support and for E‑Rate eligibility of redundant connectivity to improve network resilience. CoSN argues that screen‑time policy should remain local, opposes a federal parental opt‑out requirement, and warns that a single national screen‑time rule would harm education. CoSN opposes terminating or reducing E‑Rate, urges preservation of its framework, supports consultant participation, and rejects a federal screen‑time opt‑out tied to E‑Rate.
